title: Harden streaming metering for interleaved sideband and late-finalize protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe sporadic overcharging and missing credits when WebSocket/HTTP-Stream clients send interleaved sideband messages (attachments, function call metadata, user edits) that arrive after the server has emitted the terminal token frame. The current finalization path assumes a single canonical termination event and can: (1) double-count tokens when late sideband fragments are reattached, (2) drop input token credits when server finalizes before buffered sideband reconciliation, and (3) misattribute cost across multiplexed sessions during partial reconnects.

Goals: Define and implement a late-finalize protocol that: (a) establishes idempotent reconciliation windows for sideband fragments, (b) provides deterministic crediting semantics for midstream model switches and finalization race conditions, and (c) exposes observability/trace points to detect and debug out-of-order attribution in production.

Proposed approach:
- Introduce a five-stage finalization handshake: PREPARE -> SNAPSHOT -> ACK_FRAGMENT_SET -> FINALIZE -> POSTCHECK. Each stage is idempotent and annotated with a monotonically-increasing session nonce and a finalization epoch.
- Track a lightweight fragment manifest in the metering service for active stream sessions (manifest entries are small strings: fragment_id, kind=input|output|sideband, length_tokens, epoch). Manifests are persisted with a compact vector clock to allow detection of late fragments without full payload retention.
- On FINALIZE, compute delta between SNAPSHOT and ACK_FRAGMENT_SET; only reconcile uncovered fragments. Use provisional credits for in-flight fragments and convert to final credits after POSTCHECK. Provisional credits are visible in Console tooling as "pending" until POSTCHECK completes.
- For midstream model handoffs, record the model_variant_id in the manifest and prorate generated token credits according to the model switch boundary (provisional allocation then finalized at POSTCHECK).
- Rate-limiter integration: during PREPARE, pin the session's rate-window key to avoid window drift during reconciliation; any provisional credits exceeding quotas are marked for soft-fail and operator review rather than immediate hard-block to avoid data loss for long-running streams.

Acceptance criteria:
- No customer-reported ghost charges for interleaved sideband patterns seen in production traces (sampled from last 90 days).
- End-to-end tests that simulate out-of-order fragments, delayed sideband messages, and reconnects pass deterministically with expected final credits.
- Console shows "pending" vs "final" credits for stream sessions and exposes the finalization epoch and fragment manifest in the trace.
- Migration plan for historical sessions to avoid credit delta regressions.

Rollout plan: feature-flag behind metering-late-finalize. Beta rollout to 3% of traffic this week, 25% after stability checks, full rollout next cycle. Backstop: automatic fallback to legacy finalizer with a reconciliation audit job for affected sessions.

Risks and mitigations:
- State blowup: manifests could grow for chatty sideband clients. Mitigate with fragment TTL (default 1 hour) and compaction heuristics; large attachments are only referenced by checksum, not retained.
- Complexity in billing pipeline: add regression tests and a local deterministic simulator to validate credit algebra.

Work items (implementation phases):
1) Design and proto (this ticket) - finalize protobufs and API changes for stream protocol.
2) Server-side manifest store and finalizer FSM.
3) Metering ledger changes: provisional credit types + conversion.
4) Console/observability: show manifest and pending credits.
5) Integration tests + chaos tests (network reorder, reconnects).

Links to artifacts and tests: see attachments.
